assertion_results.text: Identifies path traversal via the unvalidated 'file' parameter
assertion_results.evidence: "Path traversal → arbitrary file read" ... "the `file` query parameter is attacker-controlled and goes straight into `open()`."

assertion_results.text: Gives the concrete exploit: ?file=../../etc/passwd (or similar) escapes /var/exports
assertion_results.evidence: "`GET /export?file=../../etc/passwd` resolves to `/var/exports/../../etc/passwd`, so the route reads files outside the exports directory."

assertion_results.text: Fix: canonicalize/confine the path to the base directory; reject .. and absolute paths
assertion_results.evidence: "resolve the path with `os.path.realpath` and reject it unless it starts with `/var/exports/`"; send_from_directory "confines the path to the base directory with Werkzeug's `safe_join`". The realpath prefix check rejects both .. and absolute-path escapes.

assertion_results.text: Rates it High/Critical with exploit + fix (and does not require JS-specific knowledge)
assertion_results.evidence: Listed under "🔴 Critical" with Exploit, Impact and Fix bullets. The answer uses only Python/Flask APIs (open, os.path.realpath, send_from_directory) and needs no JS-specific knowledge.
